text:
The story around Jake Walman is whether he has a future in Edmonton. Mike Babcock made him a healthy scratch through most of November, and the trade talk followed: HockeyFeed ran "It looks like Jake Walman is done in Edmonton," and NHL Trade Rumors called him a trade candidate. He came back on Nov. 22 in St. Louis, a 5-4 overtime loss, with four shots in 16.6 minutes.

The case against him is familiar. One assist in 12 games, ice time down more than four minutes a night, and the Oilers get 47.6% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.15 more expected goals per 60 with him on the ice last season, bottom 5% of defensemen.

The case for patience is luck. Edmonton has scored 9.4 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Walman out there, which has cost him points, and gaps like that usually swing back. The tools are still there too: a 96.7 mph shot (94th percentile) and top speed in the 96th percentile by NHL EDGE. Whether he gets the games for that luck to turn, in Edmonton or somewhere else, is the question.
